name: Gonial angle reduction (V-line surgery)

lead: V-line surgery narrows a wide lower face. Bone is removed from the gonial angle, the corner of the lower jaw, so the face tapers toward the chin. It is often paired with chin reshaping and is established in East Asian aesthetic surgery for patients with wide lower faces.

In looksmaxxing forums it sits at the opposite end from jaw implants: it removes width and angularity rather than adding it. Published evidence is mainly surgeon case descriptions and technique papers; a 1991 paper graded patients by the degree of angle protrusion and matched the resection to each type. No randomized trials were found.

paras: The operation is done through incisions inside the mouth under general anesthesia, followed by a recovery period with swelling. Some designs also take the outer cortex of the lower border and reshape the chin. Botulinum toxin in the masseter is a non-surgical option some papers describe for slimming the lower face.

Reported risks of mandibular contouring include nerve injury, bleeding, infection, asymmetry and unsatisfactory contour. Damage to the mental nerve is named as the greatest risk of jaw and chin reshaping in facial feminization literature. It is major elective surgery.

angle.text: A narrower lower face with a tapered, V-shaped jawline. Bone is shaved at the jaw angle, often with chin reshaping, and the change shows once swelling settles. It is established in East Asian aesthetic surgery, with evidence mostly from surgeon case series.

lead: Gonial angle reduction, commonly marketed as V-line surgery, is a cosmetic jaw-contouring operation in which bone is removed from the angle of the mandible, where the lower border of the jaw meets the vertical ramus, in order to narrow the lower face and give it a tapered, V-shaped outline. It is frequently paired with reshaping of the chin.[1][2]

The surgical literature on aesthetic mandibular contouring dates at least to a 1991 paper describing angle reduction and genioplasty for purely aesthetic reasons, which graded patients by the degree of angle protrusion.[2] The topic appears in later work on Asian patients seeking a slimmer lower face, as well as in facial feminization surgery, where jaw reduction is one of several procedures used to soften a masculine lower face.[3][4][5]

The evidence base consists mostly of technique descriptions and surgeon-reported case series; no randomized controlled trials were found. Reviews of the area note that surgical angle reduction is a complex procedure with significant risks and downtime, which has led some surgeons to describe less invasive options such as botulinum toxin injection into the masseter muscles.[6][1]
infobox: Gonial angle and lower border of the mandible; often chin

paras: The gonial angle is the corner of the mandible at the back of the jawline. A prominent or wide angle can make the lower face look broad or square when viewed from the front. In angle reduction, a surgeon removes part of this region through the mouth, so the outline of the jaw appears narrower.[2][6]

The 1991 classification divided patients into types A, B and C according to how far the angle protrudes. In the mildest, an angle resection alone was described; more prominent angles required additional resection of the lower border or combination with other procedures.[2] The same paper presented genioplasty, reshaping of the chin, as the second main operation used for contour change without orthodontic treatment.[2]

A related procedure, sometimes called a mini V-line, narrows the chin itself and has been described as important for achieving a feminine lower face.[7] Sliding genioplasty techniques are also used in facial feminization surgery.[5]

sections.h: Use in facial feminization and Asian aesthetic surgery
paras: Facial feminization surgery is a group of procedures intended to change male facial features toward female ones, and is performed mainly for transgender women with gender dysphoria, although some non-transgender women also seek parts of it.[3] Reviews of gender-affirming surgery list jaw and chin contouring among the procedures used.[4] The Wikipedia article on the subject says reducing the jaw can be done through the mouth and that shaving the masseter muscle can also narrow the jaw's appearance.[8]

A 2020 review describes mandible contouring for aesthetic enhancement in Asian patients, a population in which narrow, tapered lower faces are frequently requested.[1] A 2016 paper on patients with wide, short faces describes combining chin fat grafting with masseter botulinum toxin as an alternative to invasive angle reduction and genioplasty, which it characterizes as complex procedures with significant risks and downtime.[6]

Wikipedia's article on facial feminization surgery names damage to the mental nerve, which supplies sensation to the chin and lower lip, as the greatest risk of jaw and chin reshaping, and lists tooth-root injury, infection, bone non-union and injury to the mentalis muscle as further risks.[8]

The aesthetic mandibular contouring literature also treats asymmetry and unsatisfactory contour as outcomes the surgeon must plan against, and describes the operations as involving downtime and risk compared with injectable approaches.[6]

Published human data are limited to descriptive technique papers and surgeon case series, such as the 1991 aesthetic mandible contouring report and later reviews in Asian and feminization patients.[2][1][3] No randomized trial of gonial angle reduction for appearance was found. Registered trials that turn up in searches for the term concern unrelated topics such as mandibular fracture plates.[9]

In looksmaxxing forums, discussion of the jaw mostly concerns making it wider, longer and more angular through implants, orthognathic surgery or masseter growth; angle reduction is generally raised in the context of the opposite goal, a narrower or more tapered lower face, and of the contrast between East Asian and Western ideals of jaw shape. Some forum posters describe an ideal jaw in which the widest part of the mandible sits at the gonial angle and tapers into a defined chin, which is the shape V-line surgery aims to produce in a wider jaw.

lore.intro: On looksmaxxing forums the jaw is usually discussed as something to enlarge, and V-line surgery appears as the reverse option, tied to ideals of a narrow, tapered lower face.

claims.claim: A narrower, V-tapered jaw is the more attractive lower-face shape
Botulinum toxin in the masseter can give a similar slimming effect without surgery
